conviction_note: Balanced evidence. Market levels in Q3 point to asset-based fees landing at or slightly above a consensus that already models roughly 2% q/q revenue growth. Against that sit cooling BlackRock core-equity and index flows, a tough Q3 2025 sales comparison, an already-guided sustainability drag and a soft FactSet forward guide. p_up is 50 and abs_move_pct is 6.5, close to the 6.67% option-implied move, so expected_move_pct is 0. The findings sum to -0.25. That small gap is the sign of the weak negatives, not a view, and the -10% reaction to a $0.05 miss in July shows the move will be large whichever way it goes.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of about $4.99-$5.03 (Zacks $4.99, Benzinga $5.02, TickerLeague $5.03 from 8 analysts) and revenue of $880-886M. Sources: Zacks and TickerLeague via search (https://tickerleague.com/companies/MSCI/estimates, which returned 404 on fetch) and https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MSCI/earnings-forecasts. The sources agree within 1%, so the bar is treated as sourced. Q2 2026 revenue was $867.0M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001408198/000140819826000044/exhibit991earningsrelease-.htm), so the bar implies +1.5-2.2% q/q. The company gives no revenue or EPS guide, only expenses: FY26 opex $1,535-1,575M, 'towards the high end'.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 1.63% of float, roughly 1.2M shares, 1.3 days to cover, and falling 4.7% m/m (equibles, ~2026-08-19 data, https://equibles.com/stocks/msci/shortinterest), so this is not a crowded short. The baseline shows 25-delta skew +5.01 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 2.93 on only 1,668 contracts of open interest, and an ATM spread at 31% of mid, so the skew and OI are a thin signal. Event-implied move is 6.67% against a median prior reaction of 5.69% and a last reaction of -10.14%. Spot is $564.04, 20-day run-up +0.91%, 5-day -0.7%, 12.4% below the 52-week high; the stock has been flat since the July drop to about $555.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 index levels finished slightly above the June 30 base: S&P 500 +2.3%, MSCI EAFE +0.9%, MSCI EM -0.2%. Period-end AUM in ETFs linked to MSCI indexes was already $2,818B on June 30, 4.1% above the Q2 average of $2,706B on which Q2 asset-based fees of $233.1M were earned. Q3 average AUM is therefore likely about 4-7% above the Q2 average, which implies roughly +$8-12M q/q in ABF. That is consistent with, or slightly above, a consensus that needs only about +$13-19M of total revenue growth q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ABF is the line the street models off public AUM. Q2 2026 ABF rose 26.6% y/y with a record run rate, and the stock still fell 10.14% on a $0.05 EPS miss and an expense-guide raise, so ABF strength alone has not carried the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts track MSCI-linked ETF AUM, so this is mostly in the consensus. What may not be fully reflected is how far the June-end base sits above the Q2 average after a strong Q2. Revenue consensus at only +1.5-2.2% q/q leaves room for a small top-line beat. If this were fully priced, consensus revenue would sit nearer $890M.
findings.independence: The Q2 base AUM and bp fee come from the MSCI Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001408198/000140819826000044/exhibit991earningsrelease-.htm). On the Q2 call management cited 'exceptional cash flows into ETFs linked to our indexes' in early Q3 (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-msci-inc-stock/). This is a proxy: the index-return figures come from a secondary aggregator, and the BlackRock finding below points partly the other way.

findings.finding: BlackRock's Q3 2026 release (Oct 14), from MSCI's largest ABF counterparty, shows iShares ETF net inflows of $135B, down from about $178B in Q2. Core equity ETF inflows were only $3B, non-ETF index flows were -$26.1B (institutional index -$27.4B), and total AUM rose $143.6B on $205.5B of net flows, implying about -$62B of market, FX and other effects over the quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Asset-based fees and the bp fee rate were questioned on the Q2 call (fee compression from mix shift toward developed-ex-US and ACWI products). The stock fell 10.14% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since Oct 14, but the read-through to MSCI's non-ETF passive fees and core-equity ETF flows is indirect. If the market had priced a softer ABF quarter, MSCI would have weakened after Oct 14; the 5-day run-up is only -0.7%.
findings.independence: Proxy. BlackRock does not split ETF flows by index provider, and core equity includes S&P-linked funds such as IVV. The Q2 total ETF inflow figure (~$178B) comes from secondary coverage (https://www.investmentnews.com/alternatives/blackrocks-rides-to-record-153-trillion-in-assets-on-etf-and-alternatives-growth/267421). This partly offsets the index-level finding above; they are different facts.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 sustainability and expense headwinds were already guided. On the Q2 call management said Sustainability & Climate recurring net new sales would be 'roughly zero to slightly negative' over the next two quarters, with Americas cancellations a 'significant headwind'. It also put FY26 expenses 'towards the high end' of the raised $1,535-1,575M range because of First Street and AUM-linked incentive comp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 expense-guide raise and the sustainability commentary were cited in the -10.14% reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside what management guided. The residual risk is that sustainability net new turns more negative than 'slightly', or that expenses breach the high end. Neither is evidenced beyond the guide.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K shows Sustainability & Climate retention at 92.3% and net new of only $1.9M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001408198/000140819826000044/exhibit991earningsrelease-.htm). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Q3 2025 was a record Q3 for recurring sales in Index and Analytics and with hedge funds and banks (retention 94.7%), so Q3 2026 net new subscription sales face a tough y/y comparison. Analytics growth was called 'lumpy' in Q2 (organic ~7%), and management's H2 pipeline of 'large potential deals' carried an explicit warning that they may slip between quarters.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Net new subscription sales falling short of expectations drew the lead analyst question (Barclays) on the Q2 call, ahead of the -10.14% move. Q3 2025's record sales print was followed by +8.58%.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side models y/y net new sales growth. A record comparison makes positive y/y growth harder, and management's own slip warning lowers the odds the large deals land in Q3. If priced, previews would be framing Q3 sales as a likely y/y decline; none found say so.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 call commentary on pipeline lumpiness (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-21-msci-inc-stock/). Inference, not a company-level Q3 number.

findings.finding: FactSet's fiscal Q4 2026 (Jun-Aug, reported 2026-09-30) showed organic ASV +7.0% and retention above 95%, but its FY27 organic ASV guide of 5-6.5% came in below analyst expectations. That is a peer read on buy-side data budgets after MSCI last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. MSCI's Analytics segment (+9.5% subscription in Q2) competes for similar buy-side budgets.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer guide given after MSCI's July call. Consensus may not have been cut for MSCI's subscription lines, given an aggregator showing no rating changes since July. If priced, MSCI estimates would show downward revisions after Sep 30.
findings.independence: Proxy. FactSet's mix (wealth, banking, dealmakers) differs from MSCI's index and risk analytics. FactSet's own ASV growth was steady, so the signal is the forward guide only.

findings.finding: Director Rajat Taneja, an Audit Committee member, bought 1,786 shares at $560.00 (~$1.0M) on 2026-09-02, near the current $564 spot. CEO Fernandez bought 4,000 shares at ~$562 on 2026-05-15.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fernandez's 2025-26 insider buys (Feb 2026 at ~$524, May 2026 at ~$562) were not followed by uniformly positive prints: Q2 fell 10.14% after the May buy.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and public, and Form 4 buys by a director are rarely traded on. It is an open-window purchase two months into the quarter by an audit committee member, made with the stock flat since the July drop.
findings.independence: Quantisnow's insider list shows the same buy as 44 days before capture (https://quantisnow.com/insiders/MSCI). Same Form 4, so this is one finding.

findings.finding: MSCI repurchased $145M in Q2 at $557 and another $147M through July 20 at ~$558, with $1.6B left on the authorisation. With the stock near $555-565 all of Q3, continued repurchases likely lowered the share count into the EPS bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks are a routine EPS support for MSCI and have not historically moved the print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely in models. The residual is the extent of Q3 repurchases at depressed prices, which is not known until the release.

rejected_candidates.detail: The 8-K exhibit 99.1 gives retention of 95.3% against 94.4%; the 62.1% is a transcription artefact of the search snippet.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Compass Financial Technologies and Foxberry acquisitions (multi-asset index capabilities)
rejected_candidates.detail: The search result carried no date that could be tied to 2026; it may be an older deal, so it was not filed.
Management said on the Q2 call that the partnership is not yet in the reported numbers; it adds nothing to Q3 beyond the pipeline commentary in the sales finding.

baseline_tension: Roughly neutral against the +5 downside skew and a flat run-up. The skew rests on only 1,668 contracts of open interest, so it is thin, and the evidence does not clearly agree or disagree with it.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (a proxy below a broader series): the index-return ABF finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.6, because BlackRock's primary document (core equity +$3B, non-ETF index -$26B, about -$62B market/FX) partly contradicts it.
Rule 6 (inside what was guided): the sustainability/expense finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.15, because management guided both explicitly.
Rule 7: short interest was checked before filing the negatives (1.63% of float, 1.3 days to cover, not crowded), so no squeeze haircut was needed. The skew is thin on OI and was left in p_up at 50.

Rule 1: the reaction function is symmetric and large (a -10% move on a $0.05 miss, +8.6% on a record-sales quarter), so abs_move_pct stays at 6.5 and the sign uncertainty went to p_up rather than to the size.
